newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy won't consider late entry into EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy won't consider late entry into EMU.

text.p: Italy will not consider any compromise plan to allow the country to join European Monetary and Economic Union after 1999, a senior Treasury official said on Tuesday.

"The Italian government will not consider scenarios different from the commitment it has made to voters. Italy, just as it was among the founders of the European Community 40 years ago, will be among the founders of the single currency," the official told Reuters.
The official also said Italy was not aware of any compromise plan that envisioned Italy joining after 1999.
He was commenting on a Financial Times report that said Italy will be offered a deal that would delay its entry into EMU until 2000 or 2001.
The newspaper, quoting unnamed senior monetary officials, had described the deal as "a face-saving compromise designed by senior European central bankers and monetary officials.".
"Every time the prospect of Italy entering EMU becomes more concrete, people in some financial circles get a belly ache," the official said.
